evidence.detail: 30.cli-interface.srs.md:7065 (IR-CLI-113 AC-2) makes `wave status` report action counts (`due`, `interrupted`, `failed`, `sent`, `waived`, `held`) and an `attention[]` list built from action states, and :7067 (AC-4) runs the citation scan only with `--with-tests`. 50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16709 (FR-NODE-249 AC-2): "a `complete` node whose ACs are checked, covered and unexpired is `done` without the scan, and the same node with an uncited AC is `unverified` only when the scan ran." :16840 (FR-NODE-251 AC-1): `wave actions` "SHALL always run the test-citation scan ... a node whose AC no test cites is `unverified`"; :16842-16843 (AC-3, AC-4) make an action `due` only for a `done` node and `held-unverified` for an `unverified` one. No AC of IR-CLI-113 says whether its action counts come from the unscanned node state it reports or from the always-scanned state of FR-NODE-251, and IR-CLI-113 names the bucket `held` while FR-NODE-251 names the state `held-unverified`. Counter-case: a `complete` node with checked, covered, unexpired ACs, one of them cited by no test, and one `notify` with no journal line: `wave status` without `--with-tests` reports the node `done`; its action count is `due: 1` under one reading and `held: 1` under the other, while `wave actions` reports it `held-unverified`.

findings.description: The K-4 fix made `wave status` unscanned by default and `wave actions` always scanned, so the two readers can disagree on a node's state; IR-CLI-113 does not say which state its `action_counts`, summary action counts and `attention[]` use, so a test of the default `wave status` output for such a node has no single expected value, and an agent following FR-FLOW-222 AC-5 can see an action counted `due` that `wave actions` will not return.
findings.suggested_action: State in IR-CLI-113 AC-2 how action counts are derived without `--with-tests` (for example: action counts and `attention[]` always use the FR-NODE-251 state, or an action of a node whose `cited_checked` is false is counted under its own bucket), and use one name for the held state in both requirements.

evidence.detail: 60.workflow-release.srs.md:15120 (FR-FLOW-217 AC-3): "EVERY such change SHALL write a new graph version, append a `phase=\"redecompose\"` line, and pass `orchestrate wave check` and `schedule waves` before the next dispatch." 50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16771 (FR-NODE-250 AC-1): only "THE first line of a run SHALL accept an optional `graph {path, digest}`"; :16772 (AC-2) gives the `redecompose` line no graph field. 30.cli-interface.srs.md:7068 (IR-CLI-113 AC-5): the argument-free leaf "read[s] the graph named by that run's first-line `graph` reference; WHEN the file's digest differs from the recorded one it SHALL still read the file and report warning `graph-digest-mismatch`"; 50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16840 (FR-NODE-251 AC-1) finds the graph the same way; 60.workflow-release.srs.md:15438 (FR-FLOW-222 AC-1) records `graph {path, digest}` on the first line only, and :15442 (AC-5) makes `wave status` the only progress reader. Grep of docs/spec/*.srs.md for a field that records a later graph version or digest: none.

findings.description: After a sanctioned redecomposition there is no journal field that records the new graph version, so the argument-free readers either read the pre-redecomposition graph (if the new version has a new path: a node added by R3 or R4 is missing from `waves[]`, against IR-CLI-113 AC-1 "every node of the graph" and the remaining-wave read of FR-FLOW-217 AC-1) or report `graph-digest-mismatch` on every later call for the rest of the run (if the same path is overwritten), so the warning can no longer tell a hand edit from a recorded change.
findings.suggested_action: Let the `redecompose` line carry `graph {path, digest}` (FR-NODE-250 AC-2) and have IR-CLI-113 AC-5 and FR-NODE-251 AC-1 read the latest recorded graph reference of the run (first line or latest `redecompose` line), comparing the file digest against that one.
